randomized_air_hockey.notes: Paper-reported >98% online success after about 1300 of 2000 trials, with 1020 silicon neurons. These numbers are retained for provenance and are not scored targets on the local software scale.

velocity_range_extreme.notes: Paper-reported 86% online success on [0.5, 2.0] m/s, attributed to finite encoding resolution. These numbers are retained for provenance and are not scored targets on the local software scale.

velocity_range_wide.notes: Paper-reported approximately 93% asymptotic online success on [0.7, 1.5] m/s, versus 97% on [0.7, 0.9] m/s. These numbers are retained for provenance and are not scored targets on the local software scale.

_setup_note: Paper-reported numbers above are unchanged. They are late-training on-line success rates after up to 2000 trials on DYNAP-SE silicon and the authors' MuJoCo robot; final_success is the corresponding quantity here (last 500 of 2000 online trials), measured on a software spiking substrate and a substituted three-joint MuJoCo arm, so the paper values are provenance, not targets. The reference learns with Eq. 1 from a zero readout on each hidden chip; its learning rate was chosen on the public split only (method/selected_hyperparameters.json).

randomized_air_hockey.description: Online learning of interception with randomized launch position (x in [0.95, 1.05] m) and speed (1.0-1.5 m/s), the paper's main setting.

final_success.description: Fraction of successful episodes (puck past x = 1.5 m with forward speed > 0.1 m/s) among the last 500 of the 2000 online learning episodes, averaged over the hidden controller instances: the success a learner has reached within the paper's trial budget.

online_success.description: Fraction of successful episodes among all 2000 online learning episodes, averaged over the hidden controller instances (the paper's on-line success rate): how quickly success is acquired.

randomized_air_hockey.notes: Local software robot and spiking substrate, not silicon measurements. 20 hidden controller instances, each learning online for the paper's 2000 trials from a zero readout; identical launches and action draws for every method.
